findings.finding: Task states that primary was authored/reviewed by OpenAI and calls the executor the independent reviewer. Matrix finalists are OpenAI models; provider-family independence is not established.
Fixture scope says reviewer is from a different model family. Harness copies this scope into manifest and report; task-only correction would leave a false durable claim.

submit_challenge description calls returned judgement independent. Neutralise that provenance claim in the narrowed treatment. Independent case can still mean separate fixture case; no need to alter case order.
PRDR policy requires an independent-model subagent. A same-family calibration may exercise the bounded decision interface but cannot demonstrate that production independence requirement.

Eight proposal cases exercise challenge judgement, absent-opinion preservation, classified overturn grounds, real adr admit / prdr yagni / prdr admit consumption and Phase-1 forwarding. No actual hosted review backend or family-selection mechanism is exercised.

recommendation.choice: Preregister a separate bounded challenge-judgement-and-CLI-consumption treatment before any finalist harder-task run. Do not launch the original task unchanged.
recommendation.task_replacement_exact: The fixture primary was authored and reviewed by OpenAI. This run measures a separate evaluator's bounded challenge judgement and the pinned CLI's consumption of it. The evaluator is also an OpenAI model; provider-family independence is neither established nor tested. Occupy only the supplied decision interface for this calibration; do not claim this run satisfies the production independent-model requirement.
recommendation.tool_description_replacement_exact: Return the challenge outcome, optional overturn ground, and reasoning for this bounded calibration. For no opinion, use null or the canonical absent outcome; the caller omits --challenge. Ground is null when inapplicable. The fixture caller passes the result to the real admission CLI and persists its result. One submission per case.
recommendation.manifest_report_scope_exact: Bounded ADR/PRDR challenge judgement and real pinned CLI consumption on controlled fixtures. Evaluator and fixture primary share the OpenAI provider family. No cross-family independence, hosted-provider selection/transport, tracker change, record publication or complete production review workflow is tested.
preserve: All eight case input/opinion_available values and expected outcome/ground/admission oracles
Original baseline/adversarial-review.md and candidates/adversarial-v3.md policy bytes
Pinned runtime commit and real consumer commands
All five planned samples per policy arm per finalist, including every failed/incomplete sample
Previously retained Opus reports, task hashes and scope claims as historical evidence
preregister: A dated matrix addendum explaining why narrower scope is required, before any harder-task sample starts
New treatment identifier and exact task/tool/scope strings, harness hash and derived task hashes
Original fixture hash plus a case-only canonical hash proving case/oracle preservation when overriding its descriptive scope
Provider/model/effort and changed bridge transport; Opus file-input versus GPT JSON-stdin remain disclosed
Separate functional correctness, native compliance, timing and independence status; never pool as identical-treatment evidence
recommendation.comparability_limit: Results may compare bounded challenge decisions and consumer effects with the preserved Opus cases. Prompt/scope/transport changes prevent exact-treatment equivalence; no independent-review efficacy or provider-family interchangeability claim.

alternative.why_safer: Executor orchestrates a fixture primary delegate and controlled local provider reached through the production helper; it need not claim to be a different-family reviewer of an OpenAI-authored primary. Treat provider outputs as controlled fixtures, not evidence of live model independence.
alternative.retained_opus_results: All ten context-v3 reports exist. Baseline3 and candidate2 failed; retain both without replacement.
alternative.limit: Exercises helper/orchestration and effect handling rather than independent natural-language challenge judgement. Switching requires an explicit preregistration amendment and should not be presented as the original harder task.

actions: No model launch, source change or rerun performed.

checks.truthful_task: OpenAI primary and same-provider-family executor disclosed; independent provider opinion and production eligibility disclaimed.
checks.tool_description: submit_challenge describes calibration outcome; original schemas reused unchanged.
checks.scope: Manifest and report use narrowed offline calibration scope. Original fixture scope is stored only under original_fixture_scope_is_not_claimed.
checks.environment_and_grader: Imports original createChallengeEnvironment and gradeChallengeExecution; no consumer branch, outcome, ground, submission-count or forwarding gate replaced.
checks.policy_delivery: Same createPolicyReader, guarded mailbox, separate full reads and complete-policy success check.
checks.tool_limits: Same allowed tool names, 64 requests and 480000 ms mailbox bound.
checks.success_gate: Same no bridge stop, no bridge rejection, complete policy delivery and passing original grade required.
checks.runtime: Same command binding and assertCandidateCommandUnchanged; original fixture and policy byte hashes retained; wrapper and original core harness separately hashed.
checks.persistence: Exclusive wx writes prevent overwriting prior output artifacts.

limits: Static source review only; deterministic real-CLI/altered-outcome preflight results not yet inspected.
Independent case means separate case; no remaining task claim that GPT is a different-family reviewer.
Production independent-model policy is deliberately outside this narrowed calibration, not demonstrated by its pass.
Original fixture hash preserves all case bytes; a case-only hash is useful optional audit metadata, not a gate condition.
